messages.subject: Using external peaklist
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've been playing around with the Cardinal MSI package a little and would like to try some of the data analysis features on some older data without re-doing all the peaklists etc. Is there a way to simply coerce an R data.frame into a peaks class in Cardinal? For instance, my data frame has columns of Sample Name, X, Y, Peaks[1...n]. This would save me some time.

Heath Patterson
Chaurand Group
University of Montreal

messages.subject: Re: Using external peaklist
messages.body_plain:
Hi Heath,

Thank you for using Cardinal!

Does the code below reproduce a similar data.frame as yours?

df <- data.frame(sample=rep(c("A","B"), each=9), expand.grid(x=1:3, y=1:3),
 peak1=rnorm(18), peak2=rnorm(18), peak3=rnorm(18))

If so, then you should be able to do (for example):

msset <- MSImageSet(spectra=t(df[,4:6]), coord=df[c("x","y","sample")])

where the 'spectra' argument needs to be a matrix with each column as a mass spectrum / peaks for a single pixel.

Please note that the 'sample' column must be named 'sample' (in lower case), and it should probably be left out if you only one sample.

If you have a column for the m/z values, add an argument 'mz' and set it to that column, too, or Cardinal will simply automatically generate mz=1,2,3...

To make sure Cardinal recognizes the dataset has peaks instead of a full spectra, do:

centroided(msset) <- TRUE

If you have multiple samples, remember to consider that when plotting images:

image(msset, mz=1, subset=sample %in% "A") # plot sample 'A'
image(msset, mz=1, layout=c(1,2)) # plot both samples

Let us know if your data.frames are different or if this doesn't work for you.

Thank you,
Kyle
